issues.description: The problem statement requires make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (including the depolarization parameter p), but the template's msd.py defines make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) without the p parameter. The solution implementation includes the p parameter. This mismatch is structural and will confuse or block students (e.g., when calling teleport_s or simulating noise).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter p: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, and update its docstring accordingly. Ensure calls elsewhere in the template use the p parameter consistently (e.g., teleport_s and simulation helpers).

This mismatch creates a mapping confusion for students (the docstring in the template even documents parameter 'p'), and will cause tests or student implementations that follow the problem specification to fail or be unclear about where to pass the noise strength.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's make_y_state function signature to include the depolarization parameter 'p' (e.g., def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None:) and ensure the docstring and any calls in the template align with that parameter.
